summary: Represents a WebRTC peer and outputs a table of peer-to-peer connections, including UUID, connection state, signaling state, ICE connection state, and ICE gathering state.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Allow connecting to peers and sending media/data; disabling closes existing connections

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Reset the peer, equivalent to deactivating and reactivating

key_params.name: bitratelimits
key_params.note: Enable custom bitrate limits for associated tracks

key_params.name: minbitrate
key_params.note: Minimum bitrate in kbps for tracks

key_params.name: maxbitrate
key_params.note: Maximum bitrate in kbps for tracks

key_params.name: stun
key_params.note: STUN server URL for ICE negotiation

key_params.name: turn0server
key_params.note: First TURN server URL in the TURN server sequence

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: Each connection gets a generated UUID that must be passed to connection-level WebRTC Python methods.
The DAT manages connection/signaling state; audio and video media flow through Video Stream In/Out TOPs and Audio Stream In/Out CHOPs.
Failed ICE connection state often points to NAT traversal trouble; a TURN server may be required when STUN is insufficient.
Deactivating Active closes existing connections, so do not use it as a harmless pause switch.
Custom bitrate limits apply to all tracks associated with the WebRTC DAT.
build_relevance: 2022.24140+ WebRTC peer state and ICE signaling
key_concepts: WebRTC DAT represents a peer and outputs one table row per peer-to-peer connection UUID.
The output table exposes connection, signaling, ICE connection, and ICE gathering states for debugging.
STUN and TURN settings support ICE traversal when direct peer connectivity fails.
Media tracks are handled by Video/Audio Stream In and Out operators while this DAT manages connection state.
